correctness.rationale: For every integer m>=2, binary carry transitions give T=2r(s) for an invertible prefix-parity transform. The exact generating polynomial of r(s) is (1+z)(1+...+z^(2^(m-1)-1)), establishing every pair-weight multiplicity. Positive coordinate weights give the complete span rank without relying on enumeration. The Cayley graph has precisely the cosets of the generated span as components. Exhaustive direct enumerator and rank checks pass for all 1016 affine words at m=2,...,8; finite checks are corroboration, not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The claim identifies the complete flat pair-weight distribution and every rank step for a classical infinite code family under a newly studied protection invariant, producing an explicit connected-component staircase and a sharp 3n/4 transition. These facts address the natural gap between a general abstract pair-generation criterion and a concrete code family, not a single numerical or routine finite case.
